prompt: Two parallel curbs are crossed by a straight sewer line. One interior angle measures $(3x + 15)^\circ$, and the co-interior angle beside it (same side of the sewer line) measures $(2x + 25)^\circ$. Find the measure, in degrees, of the FIRST angle.
hint: Co-interior angles on parallel lines are supplementary — set the sum to $180^\circ$.

hints.text: Co-interior angles on parallel lines are supplementary — set the sum to $180^\circ$.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try plain numbers first: co-interior angles of $x$ and $50^\circ$ on parallel lines give $x + 50 = 180$, so $x = 130$. Your version just adds two expressions before setting the sum to $180$.
$5x + 40 = 180$ gives $x = 28$, so the first angle is $3(28) + 15 = 99^\circ$.

explanation: Because the curbs are parallel, the co-interior angles add to $180^\circ$: $(3x + 15) + (2x + 25) = 180$.
Substitute into the expression the question asked about: $3(28) + 15 = 84 + 15 = 99^\circ$.
Check: the other angle is $2(28) + 25 = 81^\circ$, and $99 + 81 = 180$. ✓

alternativeExplanations.title: Finish with the partner angle
steps: If you find the second angle first, $2(28) + 25 = 81^\circ$, you are one subtraction from done.
The pair is supplementary, so the first angle is $180 - 81 = 99^\circ$.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: The trap answer is 28. That is $x$ — a helper number — and the question asked for a MEASURE in degrees.

A second trap is setting the expressions equal ($3x + 15 = 2x + 25$, giving $x = 10$), which treats co-interior angles as congruent. They are supplementary. Sum to 180, solve, then substitute back: 99.
